name: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia
theme: watch-and-wait modeled as a ranked arm

meta.title: CLL in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia / small lymphocytic lymphoma (adult)
meta.population: Adults; early-stage observation, treatment-naive active disease, and relapsed/refractory settings. Richter transformation is a scope boundary (named, not ranked).
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for CLL - the disease where the first ranked option is often to do nothing yet: watch-and-wait remains the standard for inactive early-stage disease because even a modern BTK inhibitor improved event-free but not overall survival there (CLL12, stated verbatim). Once iwCLL-active, the modern menu is chemo-free: fixed-duration venetoclax-obinutuzumab vs continuous BTK inhibition, with TP53 status as the master durability lever and cardiac history gating first-generation ibrutinib. Display rule: PFS and OS fractions pool for ranking at stated horizons (declar…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic patient. Training only. Not medical advice.
meta.classification: WHO-HAEM5 (2022) CLL/SLL; iwCLL 2018 diagnostic and treatment-indication criteria
meta.response: iwCLL 2018 response criteria; uMRD (<1e-4) after fixed-duration therapy

stages.label: Presentation & activity
stages.question: Is this CLL active by iwCLL criteria - or is watching the treatment?
stages.decision: Apply the iwCLL 2018 treatment indications; inactive disease is observed, actively.

stages.label: Biology & gates
stages.question: TP53 status, IGHV status, cardiac history - the three routing tests.
stages.decision: Resolve del(17p)/TP53 before any frontline choice; IGHV informs durability; cardiac history gates first-generation BTKi.

stages.label: Frontline plan
stages.question: Fixed-duration or continuous - and what does each buy this biology?
stages.decision: Rank the chemo-free menu: venetoclax-obinutuzumab (12 months, then stop) vs acalabrutinib-based (continuous) vs legacy options.

stages.label: End-of-treatment MRD
stages.question: After fixed-duration therapy: how deep is the remission?
stages.decision: uMRD after venetoclax-obinutuzumab predicts remission durability; detectable MRD sharpens surveillance.

stages.label: Relapsed / refractory
stages.question: What was used before - and what does that leave?
stages.decision: Sequence by prior exposure: venetoclax-rituximab, next-generation BTKi, noncovalent pirtobrutinib after covalent failure, CAR-T after double exposure.

stages.label: Trial matching
stages.question: Which studies fit this biology and exposure history?

stages.label: Data artifacts
stages.question: Which result moves the plan most?
stages.decision: Rank artifacts by live VOI flips.

Patient.label: Age
Patient.help: A modifier, plus the FCR eligibility bound (<=65, fit) for the historical IGHV-mutated plateau option.
Patient.helpPatient: CLL is mostly a disease of later life; the modern options were built for that.

Patient.label: Performance status (ECOG)
Patient.help: Modifier only; the chemo-free menu tolerates frailty far better than the chemoimmunotherapy era did.
Patient.helpPatient: Day-to-day energy - the modern treatments are built to preserve it.

Patient.label: Comorbidity burden
Patient.help: CLL14 was built FOR the high-comorbidity patient (median CIRS 8) - burden shifts numbers, not eligibility, on the modern menu. FCR requires low burden.
Patient.helpPatient: Other health problems matter less on the modern options than they used to.

Diagnostic gates.label: iwCLL treatment indication
Diagnostic gates.help: The iwCLL 2018 criteria (progressive marrow failure, massive/progressive nodes or spleen, doubling time, symptoms). Inactive disease ranks observation FIRST - CLL12 showed even modern early intervent…
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: Whether the CLL is actually causing trouble. If not, watching closely IS the treatment - proven, not passive.

Diagnostic gates.label: del(17p) / TP53 status
Diagnostic gates.help: The master durability lever: TP53 disruption shortens fixed-duration remissions and leans the choice continuous. Ranking is withheld while pending - this test changes the answer.
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: One gene test that shapes which plan lasts longest - worth waiting days for.

Diagnostic gates.label: IGHV mutation status
Diagnostic gates.help: Mutated IGHV is the biology where FCR produced its long-term plateau (CLL8) and where fixed-duration remissions run longest; unmutated applies a durability modifier.
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: A once-ever test of the leukemia's ancestry that predicts how long remissions last.

Diagnostic gates.label: Cardiac history
Diagnostic gates.help: Atrial fibrillation/anticoagulation history gates first-generation ibrutinib; ALPINE showed zanubrutinib beats it head-to-head with fewer cardiac events, and ELEVATE-TN excluded significant cardiovas…
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: Heart history picks WHICH pill, not whether there is one.

On treatment.label: MRD at end of fixed-duration therapy
On treatment.help: The fixed-duration report card (CLL14): uMRD predicts long treatment-free remission; detectable MRD sharpens surveillance - re-treatment still waits for iwCLL activity.
On treatment.helpPatient: The deep test at the end of the one-year course that predicts how long the treatment-free stretch lasts.

On treatment.label: Prior therapy exposure
On treatment.help: The relapse menu is exposure-routed: venetoclax-rituximab needs venetoclax-naivety, pirtobrutinib exists FOR covalent-BTKi failure, liso-cel for double exposure.
On treatment.helpPatient: What was used before decides what is strongest next.

Where you are.label: months since diagnosis
Where you are.help: Twin clock: places 'you are here' on the months-from-diagnosis axis. Not read by the engine (completeness_only).
Where you are.helpPatient: How long since your diagnosis - marks where you are on the modelled journey.

Where you are.label: Your state (optional)
Where you are.help: Only used to list cancer centres near you. Leave blank to see national results.
Where you are.helpPatient: Only used to list cancer centres near you. Leave blank to see national results.

Newly diagnosed.name: Watch and wait (active observation)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: iwCLL 2018 / NCCN v2.2026 standard for inactive disease
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none - and the anxiety of watching is named, not dismissed
Newly diagnosed.patient: Watching closely IS the treatment: a placebo-controlled trial of a modern drug could not beat it where it counts.

Newly diagnosed.name: Venetoclax + obinutuzumab (12 months, then stop)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: grade 3-4 neutropenia 52.8%; TLS ramp managed; then treatment-free
Newly diagnosed.patient: One year of treatment, then none: infusions up front, a daily pill for the rest of the year, and then a planned stop.

Newly diagnosed.name: Acalabrutinib +/- obinutuzumab (continuous)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN v2.2026 preferred continuous frontline; leans forward for TP53-disrupted disease
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: headache early, bruising; fewer cardiac events than first-generation BTKi
Newly diagnosed.patient: A daily pill that keeps working as long as you take it - the trade is an open-ended calendar for excellent control.

Newly diagnosed.name: Ibrutinib (first-generation, continuous)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: historical standard; later-generation BTKis preferred on tolerability (NCCN v2.2026)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: atrial fibrillation, hypertension, bleeding - the reasons the next generation exists
Newly diagnosed.patient: The pill that changed this disease - now usually passed over for its gentler successors, and gated entirely by heart history.

Newly diagnosed.name: FCR chemoimmunotherapy (historical, IGHV-mutated fit patients)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: largely retired (NCCN v2.2026); the plateau lesson is why IGHV is still tested
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: prolonged neutropenia 16.6% first year; secondary malignancies 13.1% - the price of the plateau
Newly diagnosed.patient: The old six-month chemotherapy that, for one specific biology, sometimes never needed a round two - kept here as the lesson it is.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.patient: In this slow disease, even the no-treatment road is measured in years - stated honestly, alongside the better ones.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Venetoclax + rituximab (fixed duration)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN v2.2026 preferred for venetoclax-naive relapse
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The fixed-duration relapse option: two years, then a planned stop.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Zanubrutinib (next-generation BTKi, continuous)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN v2.2026 preferred BTKi for BTKi-naive relapse
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: neutropenia; fewer cardiac events than ibrutinib
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The pill that beat the original pill in a straight head-to-head - including on heart safety.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Pirtobrutinib (noncovalent BTKi, after covalent failure)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN v2.2026 option after covalent BTKi failure
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: infections, bruising; notably low BTKi-class cardiac rates
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A differently-shaped version of the same pill class, built for when the first shape stops working.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Lisocabtagene maraleucel (CAR-T, double-exposed)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: CRS and neurotoxicity; a hospital-anchored undertaking
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The cell-therapy option for when both pill classes have failed - honest numbers: deep remissions happen, for about one in five.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Comfort first - in a slow disease, still a road measured in seasons, not days.

milestones.title: IGHV + TP53/del(17p) BEFORE first treatment
review: IGHV mutation status + TP53/del(17p) BEFORE first treatment - they pick the whole road (FCR's niche is IGHV-mutated/TP53-intact ONLY; TP53-aberrant leans continuous-BTKi…
iwCLL treatment indication met? if not - watch-and-wait stands even against a positive-EFS trial (CLL12 firsthand)
fixed-duration (ven-obi 12mo, ven-R 24mo) vs continuous (BTKi) is the modern fork - patient priorities decide
at relapse: WHAT was used and HOW it ended (BTKi progression vs intolerance; covalent vs non-covalent; double-refractory routes to CAR-T)

honesty: Unverified statuses never carry the current date; every 'confirm' is in the manifest staleness list.
Watch-and-wait renders as a ranked, evidence-backed treatment - with CLL12's own conclusion quoted: EFS moved, the standard did not.
PFS and OS fractions pool for ranking at stated horizons (declared teaching rule, horizon chip on every card); response rates (ORR, CR) display with labels and never rank.
The fixed-duration and continuous calendars render side by side - the trade is shape-of-life, and the trainer never pretends one calendar is free.
MRD plans surveillance, never re-treatment: iwCLL activity criteria govern re-treatment, and the checkpoint says so.
Liso-cel's 18% CR is stated at face value - modest and real, never inflated by the word CAR-T.
The trial-matching screen renders a placeholder entry as needs-verification, never as a match.
FCR renders as the historical lesson it is: the plateau, and its counted price (secondary malignancies 13.1%).
If the trainer disagrees with the paper, trust the paper.
gates: treatment arms rank only for iwCLL-active disease; inactive disease ranks observation first
del(17p)/TP53 must be resulted before frontline ranking
significant cardiac history gates first-generation ibrutinib
Richter transformation routes out of this trainer
care: Venetoclax ramp monitoring (labs resulted within hours)

surveillance.cadence: CBC and clinical review every 3-12 months per risk; iwCLL activity criteria govern any re-treatment
